info.name: Content Platform API
info.description:
Backend API for the Content Platform learning project (Organizations, Users, Posts, Comments).

**Response envelope** — every response has the shape `{ success, data?, message?, statusCode? }`. Validation failures (400) include a specific `message` describing the first failing field.

**Errors** — `success: false` with a human-readable `message` and matching HTTP `statusCode` (400 validation, 401 auth, 403 authorization, 404 not found, 409 conflict, 429 rate-limited, 500 unexpected).

## Base URL

`http://localhost:3000/api/v1`

Every request in this collection uses `{{baseUrl}}`, which resolves from the **Content Platform - Local** environment. Select that environment from the dropdown before sending requests.

## Authentication

`POST /auth/login` and `POST /auth/register` both return two tokens:

- **`data.accessToken`** — send as `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}` on every protected request. Valid for 15 minutes.
- **`data.refreshToken`** — store it, send it in the body of `POST /auth/refresh` to get a new access token without logging in again.

This collection captures both tokens into the environment automatically on register/login (see each request's Tests tab) — every other request already reads `{{accessToken}}`, so you never copy-paste a token by hand.

`POST /auth/logout` deletes the refresh token server-side (revocation), so a stolen refresh token stops working immediately after logout.

## Authorization model

Ownership-based: only the author of a Post or Comment can update/publish/delete it (403 otherwise). Posts and Comments are scoped to the caller's Organization (from the token, never from the request body) — cross-organization access returns 404, not 403, to avoid leaking existence of other orgs' data.

## Using this collection

Run **Auth → Register** once (or **Login** if the user already exists) — `accessToken`, `refreshToken`, and `userId` are captured into the environment automatically. Creating a Post likewise saves `postId`, and creating a Comment saves `commentId`, which the matching update/publish/delete requests already use in their URLs.
